newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Oil traders to converge on Singapore for APPEC.
newsitem.headline: Oil traders to converge on Singapore for APPEC.

text.p: Oil traders from around the world are scheduled to converge on Singapore next week for the annual Asia-Pacific Petroleum Conference (APPEC).
The traders are meeting at a time of firm product and crude prices in Asia, but also when arbitrage relationships with the west are changing.
The APPEC conference starts on Monday but the bulk of the speaking schedule begins on Tuesday and closes on Wednesday.
Oil minister of OPEC heavyweight Saudi Arabia, Ali Al-Naimi, is the key ministerial speaker.
Other speakers at the conference include Patrick Thompson, president of the New York Mercantile Exchange and Andrew Hall, president of Phibro Inc.
APPEC also attracts traders and analysts from all over the world for bilateral meetings with trading partners on the sidelines of the conference.
Crude and product prices jumped this week after the United States fired two salvos of missiles at Iraq in retaliation for an incursion of Iraqi forces against the Kurds in the northern no-fly zone.
Crude prices have been supported all year, partly contributing to the weakness in refinery margins between June and August.

Refiners' profits and trading opportunities were also affected when product prices came under pressure in the middle of the year with Thailand and South Korea adding around 700,000 barrels per day of new capacity.

The increased refining capacity has reduced the potential for Asia to attract arbitrage barrels of some products, particularly from the west, which traders said was becoming a permanent feature of the Asian market.
